exposure: Enoxaparin dose (40 mg/day vs. 60 mg/day in obese patients, 40 mg/day in non-obese patients)
cohort: 90 women who underwent cesarean section (30 obese receiving 40 mg/day enoxaparin, 30 obese receiving 60 mg/day enoxaparin, and 30 non-obese receiving 40 mg/day enoxaparin)
finding: Post-cesarean obese patients had increased procoagulant potential compared to non-obese patients, and a higher dose of enoxaparin (60 mg/day) was more effective in diminishing this risk.
